subject: cat-act-2011
note: Interpretive forks: places where two readings of the source both survive. A fork is not a defect. Each entry records the readings, which one the encoding takes, why, and what in the encoding would change if it were resolved the other way. Both entries here are asserted in cat-cases.l4 at the boundary where the readings diverge, so a change of reading cannot pass silently.

entries.provision: Cat Amendment (Local Laws) Bill 2026 cl 4; Cat Act 2011 s 79(3)(f)
entries.question: Does Bill 53 CONFER a local-law power that s 79 did not previously carry, or DECLARE the scope of one it already carried?

readings.reading: The Bill confers. s 79(3)(f) as in force authorises only a local law that specifies places and prohibits absolutely; curfews and district-wide containment were beyond power, and the amendment is what makes them available.
readings.licensed_by: The words of the paragraph being replaced: 'specifying places where cats are prohibited absolutely'. The Explanatory Memorandum's own Overview, which says the Bill amends the Act 'to provide a head of power'. The Joint Standing Committee on Delegated Legislation's reported view that 'the existing powers of the Act did not permit these local laws to be made'. And the fact of the amendment itself: if the power existed, there was nothing to supply.

readings.reading: The Bill declares. s 79(3)(f) read with the general power in s 79(1) and with Interpretation Act 1984 s 43(7)-(8) already reached conditional, time-limited and district-wide prohibitions; the amendment removes doubt without changing the law.
readings.licensed_by: The Explanatory Memorandum's own words, two paragraphs after the first: 'The Bill is intended to clarify the existing legislation and ensure local governments have clearly expressed authority'. The new s 79(4) opening 'WITHOUT LIMITING subsection (3)(f)', which presupposes that (3)(f) already reaches what (4) describes. s 79(3) opening 'Without limiting subsection (1)', so the general power was never cut down by the paragraph being amended. And Interpretation Act s 43(7)(b)(ii) and 43(8)(a)(i), which permit a provision 'either unconditionally or subject to any specified condition' and application 'at all times or at a specified time'.

entries.why: Not because it is the better reading of the words — the fork is live precisely because both survive — but because it is the reading on which the Bill does something, and the encoding's job here is to show what the amendment changes. Taking FORK-3-B would make both arms of s 79 agree and the module would have nothing to report. The choice is therefore stated rather than hidden, and the boundary is asserted.
entries.materialisation: The two arms in cat-part6-local-laws.l4: `section 79(3)(f) as in force authorises the local law` requires all three of specification, prohibition and absoluteness; `section 79(3)(f) as amended by Bill 53 authorises the local law` requires only prohibition.
entries.materialised_as: cat-part6-cases.l4 § `What the Bill does, and does not, change`
entries.what_changes_if_resolved_the_other_way: On FORK-3-B the `as in force` arm would authorise the curfew and the containment local law as well, `Bill 53 changes the answer for the local law` would be FALSE for every case in the file, and the three assertions that it is TRUE would fail — so the change of reading cannot pass silently. Downstream, incident B-01 would dissolve: if the Bill declares, the local laws already made were always valid and no validating provision was needed.

history.event: Opened on first reading of the Bill and its Explanatory Memorandum. The fork exists because the memorandum asserts both readings; it is not a disagreement between us and the drafter.

entries.question: When is the duty to register, microchip and sterilise breached — at the moment the cat reaches 6 months of age, or only once the owner has failed to act with all convenient speed thereafter?

readings.reading: The duty is to ensure a state of affairs, and it is breached whenever the cat has reached 6 months and the state does not obtain. On this reading the owner of a six-month-old unmicrochipped cat is in breach on the day of the cat's half-birthday.
readings.licensed_by: The words: 'The owner of a cat that has reached 6 months of age must ensure that the cat is microchipped'. No period is stated, and the duty is expressed as ensuring a state rather than doing an act by a date.

readings.reading: The duty fixes no time, so the Interpretation Act 1984 (WA) s 63 supplies one: 'Where no time is fixed or allowed within which an act or thing shall be done, such act or thing shall be done with all convenient speed and as often as occasion arises.' The owner must register, microchip and sterilise with all convenient speed after the cat reaches 6 months, and is in breach only on failing to do so.
readings.licensed_by: Interpretation Act 1984 (WA) s 63, which applies to every written law of the State unless the contrary intention appears. Supported by the Explanatory Memorandum to the Cat Bill 2011, which describes clauses 14 and 18 as requiring the owner 'to ensure it is microchipped by 6 months of age' and 'sterilised by a veterinarian, by 6 months of age' — a compliance deadline, not an instantaneous liability. The Act also shows the drafter fixing periods where one was intended (ss 15, 20, 24 and 25 each say 'within 7 days'), which tells against reading silence in ss 5, 14 and 18 as immediacy.

entries.why: s 63 is not optional: it applies unless a contrary intention appears, and nothing in ss 5, 14 or 18 shows one. Reading FORK-2-A also produces a result the drafter cannot have intended, since a vet certificate under s 14(2) or 18(2) 'cannot apply in respect of a cat that is under 6 months of age' (ss 14(3), 18(3)) — so on FORK-2-A an owner whose cat cannot safely be microchipped is necessarily in breach for however long it takes to obtain the certificate that excuses them. FORK-2-B avoids that without straining the words.
entries.materialised_as: Situation's `the owner has proceeded with all convenient speed`, read by the three contravention rules `the owner contravenes section 5(1)`, `... section 14(1)` and `... section 18(1)`.
entries.what_changes_if_resolved_the_other_way: Delete that field and the third conjunct of each of the three contravention rules. The assertion pair on `Anne and Smudge, certified at five months` and `Anne, acting promptly, certified at five months` in cat-cases.l4 is the boundary: on FORK-2-A both are in breach, on FORK-2-B only the first is.
entries.history: Opened 2026-09-30 after a reviewer put reading B. The encoding had been written on reading A, and an incident (A-01) had been raised on the strength of it. The incident is now recorded as verified-no-defect and this fork carries what was real in it.

entries.question: Registration 'may be renewed to take effect as from 1 November in any year, within the preceding period of 21 days.' Does that period begin on 11 October or 12 October?

readings.reading: 11 October to 31 October: 21 days counted back from and including 31 October, the last day before 1 November.
readings.licensed_by: The ordinary way a period 'preceding' a date is counted in days ending on the day before that date. Interpretation Act 1984 (WA) s 61 computes time by excluding the day from which the period runs, which on this reading is 1 November.

readings.reading: 12 October to 31 October: 21 clear days before 1 November, so the period begins on the 21st day before it and 11 October falls outside.
readings.licensed_by: A reading of 'the preceding period of 21 days' as 21 whole days that must have elapsed, which is how some WA drafting treats clear-day periods.

entries.why: Nothing in the regulation or in the Interpretation Act settles it, and the difference is one day at the start of a renewal window. The more generous reading is taken because the provision confers a facility on the owner rather than imposing a liability, and because a renewal lodged on 11 October defeats nobody's interest. The choice is recorded rather than hidden precisely because it is not compelled.
entries.materialised_as: The reading is inlined in `the renewal is within the period allowed by regulation 12(2)(b)` as `DATE_DAY ... AT LEAST 11`. It is one comparison and it names the fork in its comment.
entries.what_changes_if_resolved_the_other_way: Change `AT LEAST 11` to `AT LEAST 12`, and the assertion `a renewal applied for on 11 October is in time` in cat-cases.l4 flips. That assertion exists for this purpose.
entries.history: Opened 2026-09-30 when the Cat Regulations 2012 were first read.
